title: CISA ends six free cybersecurity assessments amid budget cuts
plain: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has discontinued six free cybersecurity assessments that critical infrastructure operators previously used to evaluate operational technology (OT) security. Tatyana Bolton, executive director of the OT Cyber Coalition, attributed the cuts to severe budget redu

angles.claim: AI engineering teams inside smaller utilities now inherit an OT baselining task CISA used to do for free, with no budget line for it.
angles.audience: AI and OT engineering leads at small and mid-size utilities and water systems
angles.rank_reason: It forces an immediate governance decision, who pays and who schedules the replacement assessment, so it changes a Monday task list, not just awareness.

angles.claim: Any AI system an operator connects to OT should now assume its baseline security posture is self-reported, not federally verified, until a paid substitute is booked.
angles.audience: AI governance leads and CISOs at critical infrastructure operators
angles.rank_reason: It reaches the target reader by tying the funding cut directly to AI deployment risk, but it extends the article's claim further than the reporting supports since no AI-specific gap is documented.

angles.claim: Directors should ask this Thursday which of the six discontinued assessments their AI vendors' OT integrations depended on for their own security claims.
angles.audience: Directors and boards overseeing AI deployment in critical infrastructure
angles.rank_reason: Useful boardroom question but weaker because the six assessments are unnamed, so the claim cannot be verified or acted on precisely yet.
